### GRI 302 Energy  
In 2025, HSBC achieved a 34.5% reduction in energy consumption compared with its 2019 baseline, driven by strategic divestments and energy conservation programmes supported by enhanced metering and monitoring [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. The Group sourced 94.2% of its electricity from renewable sources in 2025, advancing toward its 2030 target of 100% renewable electricity across its own operations [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. This procurement follows RE100 principles, prioritising power purchase agreements (PPAs) where feasible; where regulatory or market constraints apply—as in France and parts of India—HSBC procures renewable electricity via utility partners, and is exploring on-site generation, direct investment in renewable assets, and private wire agreements [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132].

### GRI 303 Water  
HSBC states that, “taking into account the nature of our business, we do not consider [water sourcing and efficiency] to be a material issue for our stakeholders” [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. Nevertheless, it reports implementing water-efficiency measures—including installation of water-efficient taps and flow restrictors—and continues to track water consumption [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. No quantitative data on total water withdrawal, consumption, or intensity (e.g., m³ per FTE or per revenue) are disclosed for 2025 or any prior year.

### GRI 305 Emissions  
HSBC’s scope 1 and 2 emissions (energy and road fleet) totalled 36,617 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—a 91.2% reduction from the 2019 baseline and a 62.9% reduction from 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. Scope 2 market-based emissions were 19,919 tonnes CO₂e in 2025, down from 83,760 tonnes CO₂e in 2024 and 392,270 tonnes CO₂e in 2019 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Scope 1 emissions increased slightly to 16,698 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 (from 15,025 in 2024), attributed to an adjustment of the uplift rate to include estimated fugitive emissions from refrigerant leaks in cooling systems [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Scope 2 location-based emissions were 259,129 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. Business travel (scope 3, category 6) emissions fell to 67,019 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—75.4% below 2019 and 49.9% below 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136]. Supply chain emissions (scope 3, categories 1 and 2) totalled 973,281 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 (807,293 + 165,988), representing a 10.3% reduction against 2019 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Overall scope 1, 2 and 3 (categories 1, 2 and 6) emissions were 1,076,917 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. All emissions reporting adheres to the GHG Protocol and uses the market-based scope 2 methodology [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136].

### GRI 306 Waste  
HSBC states it “does not consider hazardous waste to be a material issue for our stakeholders” and therefore reports only on total waste produced, without disaggregating hazardous and non-hazardous volumes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It confirms continuing efforts to reduce and recycle all waste under its ‘reduce, replace, remove’ environmental approach but provides no quantitative data on total waste generated, recycled, or diverted in 2025 or prior years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
HSBC’s climate strategy is anchored in its Net Zero Transition Plan, updated in November 2025, which sets science-aligned, sector-specific financed emissions targets using IEA APS and NZE 2024 scenarios [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_65][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. For oil and gas, it targets a 14–30% absolute reduction in combined on-balance sheet financed and facilitated emissions by 2030 versus 2019 (28.5 Mt CO₂e reported in 2024, −38% vs baseline) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_116][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. For power and utilities, it targets an intensity reduction to 195–270 tCO₂e/GWh by 2030; 2024 performance was 242 tCO₂e/GWh (−18% vs 2023 baseline) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_117][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. Climate risk is integrated into governance via scenario analysis—including NGFS Phase V, IPCC and IEA-aligned long-term and stress scenarios—and informs financial planning, impairment testing, and capital allocation [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_540][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_957]. However, HSBC does not fully disclose the amount or percentage of assets vulnerable to physical or transition risks across wholesale/retail lending, equity/debt holdings, or trading positions by industry, geography, credit quality or tenor [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1072].

### Not covered in source material  
- Quantitative data on water withdrawal, consumption, or intensity (GRI 303).  
- Total hazardous and non-hazardous waste volumes, recycling rates, or diversion metrics (GRI 306).  
- Scope 3 emissions beyond categories 1 (purchased goods and services), 2 (capital goods), and 6 (business travel)—including categories such as upstream transportation, downstream use of sold products, or end-of-life treatment [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1072].  
- Detailed breakdown of energy consumption by fuel type or facility type (GRI 302).  
- Assurance level or scope for scope 1 and 2 emissions data (beyond the stated limited assurance for scope 3 category 6 and supply chain data in 2025) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138].

### Board Independence and Composition  
The Nomination & Corporate Governance Committee, acting on delegated authority from the Board, assessed and confirmed the independence of all non-executive Directors and the Group Chairman who stood for election or re-election at the 2025 Annual General Meeting (AGM) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. Non-executive Directors are appointed for an initial three-year term and typically serve two consecutive terms (six years), after which any further appointment is subject to a rolling one-year term and rigorous review against the Board’s evolving needs [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. All Directors standing for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM were elected or re-elected by shareholders [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731].

### Conflicts of Interest Management

### GRI 302 Energy  
In 2025, HSBC achieved a 34.5% reduction in energy consumption compared with its 2019 baseline, driven by strategic divestments and energy conservation programmes supported by enhanced metering and monitoring [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. The Group sourced 94.2% of its electricity from renewable sources in 2025, advancing toward its 2030 target of 100% renewable electricity across its own operations [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. This procurement follows RE100 principles, prioritising power purchase agreements (PPAs) where feasible; where regulatory or market constraints apply—as in France and parts of India—HSBC procures renewable electricity via utility partners, and is exploring on-site generation, direct investment in renewable assets, and private wire agreements [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. No breakdown of energy consumption by fuel type, facility category, or geographic market is disclosed [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132].

### GRI 303 Water  
HSBC states that, “taking into account the nature of our business, we do not consider [water sourcing and efficiency] to be a material issue for our stakeholders” [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It reports implementing water-efficiency measures—including installation of water-efficient taps and flow restrictors—and continues to track water consumption [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. However, no quantitative data on total water withdrawal, consumption, intensity (e.g., m³ per FTE or per revenue), or baseline year comparisons are disclosed for 2025 or any prior year [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
HSBC reports scope 1 and scope 2 *market-based* emissions totalling 36,617 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—a 91.2% reduction from the 2019 baseline and a 62.9% reduction from 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. This figure comprises scope 1 emissions of 16,698 tonnes CO₂e and scope 2 *market-based* emissions of 19,919 tonnes CO₂e [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Scope 2 *location-based* emissions were 259,129 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. Scope 1 emissions increased slightly from 15,025 tonnes CO₂e in 2024, attributed to an adjustment of the uplift rate to include estimated fugitive emissions from refrigerant leaks in cooling systems [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Business travel (scope 3, category 6) emissions fell to 67,019 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—75.4% below 2019 and 49.9% below 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136]. Supply chain emissions (scope 3, categories 1 and 2) totalled 973,281 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 (807,293 + 165,988), representing a 10.3% reduction against 2019 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Overall scope 1, 2 (market-based), and 3 (categories 1, 2 and 6) emissions were 1,076,917 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. All emissions reporting adheres to the GHG Protocol and explicitly applies the market-based methodology for scope 2 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136]. Data for scope 1 and 2 emissions is not stated to be subject to third-party assurance; only scope 3 category 6 and supply chain data in 2025 received independent limited assurance [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138].

### GRI 306 Waste  
HSBC states it “does not consider hazardous waste to be a material issue for our stakeholders” and therefore reports only on total waste produced, without disaggregating hazardous and non-hazardous volumes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It confirms continuing efforts to reduce and recycle all waste under its ‘reduce, replace, remove’ environmental approach but provides no quantitative data on total waste generated (tonnes), hazardous vs. non-hazardous mass, recycling rate (%), or diversion metrics for 2025 or prior years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets

### GRI 302 Energy  
In 2025, HSBC achieved a 34.5% reduction in energy consumption compared with its 2019 baseline, driven by strategic divestments and energy conservation programmes supported by enhanced metering and monitoring [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. The Group sourced 94.2% of its electricity from renewable sources in 2025, advancing toward its 2030 target of 100% renewable electricity across its own operations [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. This procurement follows RE100 principles, prioritising power purchase agreements (PPAs) where feasible; where regulatory or market constraints apply—as in France and parts of India—HSBC procures renewable electricity via utility partners, and is exploring on-site generation, direct investment in renewable assets, and private wire agreements [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. No breakdown of energy consumption by fuel type, facility category, or geographic market is disclosed [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132].

### GRI 303 Water  
HSBC states that, “taking into account the nature of our business, we do not consider [water sourcing and efficiency] to be a material issue for our stakeholders” [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It reports implementing water-efficiency measures—including installation of water-efficient taps and flow restrictors—and continues to track water consumption [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. However, no quantitative data on total water withdrawal, consumption, intensity (e.g., m³ per FTE or per revenue), or baseline year comparisons are disclosed for 2025 or any prior year [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
HSBC reports scope 1 and scope 2 *market-based* emissions totalling 36,617 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—a 91.2% reduction from the 2019 baseline and a 62.9% reduction from 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. This figure comprises scope 1 emissions of 16,698 tonnes CO₂e and scope 2 *market-based* emissions of 19,919 tonnes CO₂e [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Scope 2 *location-based* emissions were 259,129 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. Scope 1 emissions increased slightly from 15,025 tonnes CO₂e in 2024, attributed to an adjustment of the uplift rate to include estimated fugitive emissions from refrigerant leaks in cooling systems [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Business travel (scope 3, category 6) emissions fell to 67,019 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—75.4% below 2019 and 49.9% below 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136]. Supply chain emissions (scope 3, categories 1 and 2) totalled 973,281 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 (807,293 + 165,988), representing a 10.3% reduction against 2019 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Overall scope 1, 2 (market-based), and 3 (categories 1, 2 and 6) emissions were 1,076,917 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. All emissions reporting adheres to the GHG Protocol and explicitly applies the market-based methodology for scope 2 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136]. Data for scope 1 and 2 emissions is not stated to be subject to third-party assurance; only scope 3 category 6 and supply chain data in 2025 received independent limited assurance [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138].

### GRI 306 Waste  
HSBC states it “does not consider hazardous waste to be a material issue for our stakeholders” and therefore reports only on total waste produced, without disaggregating hazardous and non-hazardous volumes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It confirms continuing efforts to reduce and recycle all waste under its ‘reduce, replace, remove’ environmental approach but provides no quantitative data on total waste generated (tonnes), hazardous vs. non-hazardous mass, recycling rate (%), or diversion metrics for 2025 or prior years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
HSBC’s climate strategy is anchored in its Net Zero Transition Plan, updated in November 2025, which sets science-aligned, sector-specific financed emissions targets using IEA APS and NZE 2024 scenarios [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_65][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. However, HSBC does not fully disclose the amount or percentage of assets vulnerable to physical or transition risks across wholesale/retail lending, equity/debt holdings, or trading positions by industry, geography, credit quality or tenor [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1072].

The Nomination & Corporate Governance Committee, acting on delegated authority from the Board, confirmed the independence of all non-executive Directors and the Group Chairman who stood for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. This assessment considered all circumstances likely to impair, or appear to impair, independence, in accordance with the UK and Hong Kong Corporate Governance Codes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Non-executive Directors serve initial three-year terms and typically two consecutive terms (six years); appointments beyond six years are subject to rolling one-year terms and rigorous review against the Board’s evolving needs [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. All Directors standing for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM were elected or re-elected by shareholders [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731].

### Conflicts of Interest Management  
HSBC maintains an annually reviewed conflicts of interest policy and procedures [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Directors must notify the Board of actual or potential conflicts and update it on changes to relevant facts or circumstances [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. They review and confirm their own and their closely associated persons’ outside interests twice yearly [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_733]. All conflicts are recorded in a formal register, and the Board authorised conflicts as they arose during 2025 under the Companies Act 2006 and HSBC Holdings’ Articles of Association [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Non-executive Directors undergo triennial re-vetting by the Group’s compliance team, including refreshed conflict checks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_733].

### Anti-Corruption and Integrity Framework  
HSBC’s global financial crime policy prohibits bribery and corruption and requires activity to be reasonable, transparent, appropriately documented, and authorised at an appropriate seniority level [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_174]. Risk-based due diligence and ongoing monitoring of customers and third parties are used to mitigate bribery and corruption risks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. ### Board Independence and Composition  
The Nomination & Corporate Governance Committee, acting on delegated authority from the Board, confirmed the independence of all non-executive Directors and the Group Chairman who stood for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. This assessment considered all circumstances likely to impair, or appear to impair, independence, in accordance with the UK and Hong Kong Corporate Governance Codes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Non-executive Directors serve initial three-year terms and typically two consecutive terms (six years); appointments beyond six years are subject to rolling one-year terms and rigorous review against the Board’s evolving needs [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. All Directors standing for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM were elected or re-elected by shareholders [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731].

### Conflicts of Interest Management  
HSBC maintains an annually reviewed conflicts of interest policy and procedures [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Directors must notify the Board of actual or potential conflicts and update it on changes to relevant facts or circumstances [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. They review and confirm their own and their closely associated persons’ outside interests twice yearly [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_733]. All conflicts are recorded in a formal register, and the Board authorised conflicts as they arose during 2025 under the Companies Act 2006 and HSBC Holdings’ Articles of Association [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Non-executive Directors undergo triennial re-vetting by the Group’s compliance team, including refreshed conflict checks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_733].

### Anti-Corruption and Integrity Framework  
HSBC’s global financial crime policy prohibits bribery and corruption and requires activity to be reasonable, transparent, appropriately documented, and authorised at an appropriate seniority level [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_174]. Risk-based due diligence and ongoing monitoring of customers and third parties are used to mitigate bribery and corruption risks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. In 2025, 99% of permanent and non-permanent employees completed mandatory financial crime training, including anti-bribery and corruption content — consistent with the 2024 rate [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. There were no concluded legal cases regarding bribery or corruption brought against HSBC or its employees in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175].

### Climate Risk Governance and Oversight  
The Board holds overall supervisory responsibility for HSBC’s ESG strategy, including climate risk governance, overseeing executive management on development, execution, and reporting [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_529]. The Group Chief Risk and Compliance Officer is the senior manager responsible for climate risk under the UK Senior Managers Regime [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_529]. The Group Risk Committee and Group Risk Management Meeting receive quarterly updates on climate risk indicators and oversee the Group’s climate risk profile and appetite [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_530]. The Group’s climate risk appetite statement forms part of the overarching risk appetite statement, is approved and overseen by the Board, and is reviewed annually—or sooner if breached [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_530].

### Whistleblowing and Speak-Up Mechanisms  
HSBC operates HSBC Confidential, a global whistleblowing channel managed by an independent third party in most markets, offering 24/7 hotlines and a multilingual web portal [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. In 2025, 1,100 concerns were investigated through this channel (2024: 925); 34% were substantiated (2024: 35%), and a further 19% identified other issues (2024: 22%) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. The Group Audit Committee oversees the effectiveness of the whistleblowing framework [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175].

Quantitative baselines for the conflict register (e.g., % of Directors with fully updated disclosures in 2025) and absolute employee headcount for training metrics are absent. No mention is made of GRI 2 General Disclosures requirements related to Board committee charters, evaluation methodologies, or diversity disclosures beyond gender and Black heritage representation at senior leadership level [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_614].

### GRI 302 Energy  
In 2025, HSBC reduced energy consumption by 34.5% versus its 2019 baseline, driven by strategic divestments and energy conservation programmes supported by enhanced metering and monitoring [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. The Group sourced 94.2% of its electricity from renewable sources in 2025, advancing toward its 2030 target of 100% renewable electricity across its own operations [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. Procurement follows RE100 principles, prioritising power purchase agreements where feasible; where regulatory or market constraints apply—as in France and parts of India—renewable electricity is procured via utility partners [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. No quantitative data on total energy consumption (kWh), fuel-type breakdown, or facility-category allocation is disclosed for 2025 or prior years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138].

### GRI 303 Water  
HSBC states that, “taking into account the nature of our business, we do not consider [water sourcing and efficiency] to be a material issue for our stakeholders” [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It reports installing water-efficient taps and flow restrictors and continues to track consumption [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. However, no quantitative data on total water withdrawal (m³), consumption (m³), or intensity metrics are disclosed for 2025, 2024, or 2019 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
HSBC’s scope 1 and scope 2 *market-based* emissions totalled 36,617 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—a 91.2% reduction from the 2019 baseline and a 62.9% reduction from 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. This comprises scope 1 emissions of 16,698 tonnes CO₂e and scope 2 *market-based* emissions of 19,919 tonnes CO₂e [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Scope 2 *location-based* emissions were 259,129 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—disclosed separately and excluded from the 36,617-tonne total, consistent with GHG Protocol market-based reporting [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. The scope 1 increase from 15,025 tonnes CO₂e in 2024 reflects an uplift rate adjustment to include estimated fugitive emissions from refrigerant leaks—not increased operational activity [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Business travel (scope 3, category 6) emissions fell to 67,019 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—75.4% below 2019 and 49.9% below 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136]. Supply chain emissions (scope 3, categories 1 and 2) totalled 973,281 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 (807,293 + 165,988), representing a 10.3% reduction against 2019 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Overall scope 1, 2 (market-based), and 3 (categories 1, 2 and 6) emissions were 1,076,917 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. All emissions reporting adheres to the GHG Protocol; only scope 3 category 6 and supply chain data in 2025 received independent limited assurance [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138].

### GRI 306 Waste  
HSBC states it “does not consider hazardous waste to be a material issue for our stakeholders” and reports only on total waste produced, without disaggregating hazardous and non-hazardous volumes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It confirms continuing efforts to reduce and recycle all waste under its ‘reduce, replace, remove’ approach but provides no quantitative data on total waste generated (tonnes), recycling rate (%), or intensity metrics for 2025 or prior years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
HSBC’s climate strategy is anchored in its Net Zero Transition Plan, published in November 2025, setting science-aligned, sector-specific financed emissions targets informed by IEA APS and NZE 2024 scenarios [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_65][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. For oil and gas, it targets a 14–30% absolute reduction in combined on-balance sheet financed and facilitated emissions by 2030 versus 2019; 2024 performance was 28.5 Mt CO₂e (−38% vs baseline) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_116][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. For power and utilities, it targets an intensity of 195–270 tCO₂e/GWh by 2030; 2024 performance was 242 tCO₂e/GWh (−18% vs 2023 baseline) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_117][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. Climate risk is integrated into governance via scenario analysis—including NGFS Phase V, IPCC and IEA-aligned long-term and stress scenarios—and informs financial planning and impairment testing [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_540][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_957]. However, HSBC does not fully disclose the amount or percentage of assets vulnerable to physical or transition risks across wholesale/retail lending, equity/debt holdings, or trading positions by industry, geography, credit quality or tenor [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1072].

### GRI 302 Energy  
In 2025, HSBC reduced energy consumption by 34.5% versus its 2019 baseline, driven by strategic divestments and energy conservation programmes supported by enhanced metering and monitoring [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. The Group sourced 94.2% of its electricity from renewable sources in 2025, advancing toward its 2030 target of 100% renewable electricity across its own operations [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. Procurement follows RE100 principles, prioritising power purchase agreements where feasible; where regulatory or market constraints apply—as in France and parts of India—renewable electricity is procured via utility partners [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132]. No quantitative data on total energy consumption (kWh), fuel-type breakdown, or facility-category allocation is disclosed for 2025 or prior years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138].

### GRI 303 Water  
HSBC states that, “taking into account the nature of our business, we do not consider [water sourcing and efficiency] to be a material issue for our stakeholders” [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It reports installing water-efficient taps and flow restrictors and continues to track consumption [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. However, no quantitative data on total water withdrawal (m³), consumption (m³), or intensity metrics are disclosed for 2025, 2024, or 2019 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
HSBC’s scope 1 and scope 2 *market-based* emissions totalled 36,617 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—a 91.2% reduction from the 2019 baseline and a 62.9% reduction from 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135]. This comprises scope 1 emissions of 16,698 tonnes CO₂e and scope 2 *market-based* emissions of 19,919 tonnes CO₂e [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Scope 2 *location-based* emissions were 259,129 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—disclosed separately and excluded from the 36,617-tonne total, consistent with GHG Protocol market-based reporting [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. The scope 1 increase from 15,025 tonnes CO₂e in 2024 reflects an uplift rate adjustment to include estimated fugitive emissions from refrigerant leaks—not increased operational activity [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Business travel (scope 3, category 6) emissions fell to 67,019 tonnes CO₂e in 2025—75.4% below 2019 and 49.9% below 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_135][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136]. Supply chain emissions (scope 3, categories 1 and 2) totalled 973,281 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 (807,293 + 165,988), representing a 10.3% reduction against 2019 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_136][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_137]. Overall scope 1, 2 (market-based), and 3 (categories 1, 2 and 6) emissions were 1,076,917 tonnes CO₂e in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138]. All emissions reporting adheres to the GHG Protocol; only scope 3 category 6 and supply chain data in 2025 received independent limited assurance [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_138].

### GRI 306 Waste  
HSBC states it “does not consider hazardous waste to be a material issue for our stakeholders” and reports only on total waste produced, without disaggregating hazardous and non-hazardous volumes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068]. It confirms continuing efforts to reduce and recycle all waste under its ‘reduce, replace, remove’ approach but provides no quantitative data on total waste generated (tonnes), recycling rate (%), or intensity metrics for 2025 or prior years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
HSBC’s climate strategy is anchored in its Net Zero Transition Plan, published in November 2025, setting science-aligned, sector-specific financed emissions targets informed by IEA APS and NZE 2024 scenarios [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_65][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. For oil and gas, it targets a 14–30% absolute reduction in combined on-balance sheet financed and facilitated emissions by 2030 versus 2019; 2024 performance was 28.5 Mt CO₂e (−38% vs baseline) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_116][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. For power and utilities, it targets an intensity of 195–270 tCO₂e/GWh by 2030; 2024 performance was 242 tCO₂e/GWh (−18% vs 2023 baseline) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_117][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_113]. Climate risk is integrated into governance via scenario analysis—including NGFS Phase V, IPCC and IEA-aligned long-term and stress scenarios—and informs financial planning and impairment testing [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_540][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_957]. However, HSBC does not fully disclose the amount or percentage of assets vulnerable to physical or transition risks across wholesale/retail lending, equity/debt holdings, or trading positions by industry, geography, credit quality or tenor [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1072].

### Not covered in source material  
- Total water withdrawal (m³) and consumption (m³) for 2025 and 2019, and associated intensity metrics [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].  
- Total hazardous and non-hazardous waste generated (tonnes) and recycling rate (%) for 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1068].  
- Scope 3 emissions beyond categories 1, 2, and 6 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1072].  
- Breakdown of energy consumption by fuel type or facility type [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_132].  
- Quantitative exposure of credit, equity, debt, or trading portfolios to physical and transition risks by sector, geography, credit quality, or average tenor [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_1072].

### GRI 403 Occupational Health & Safety  
HSBC reported 10 major injuries to employees in 2025 — defined as fractures, dislocations, concussions, loss of consciousness, or overnight hospital admission [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746]. The all-injury rate was 96 per 100,000 employees, up from 91 in 2024 and down from 110 in 2023 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746]. Lost days due to work injury totalled 331 in 2025, compared with 335 in 2024 and 594 in 2023 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746]. No workplace fatalities were recorded in 2025, 2024, or 2023, as the fatality rate is reported as “—” for all three years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746]. In 2025, 33 named storms affected 2,222 buildings with no injuries or impact reported [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746].

### GRI 404 Training  
In 2025, HSBC colleagues completed 5.6 million training hours, down from 6.2 million in 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_160]. This equated to 26.8 training hours per full-time equivalent (FTE) employee, versus 29.6 hours per FTE in 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_160]. Mandatory conduct training was completed by 99% of employees in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_66]. The Digital Acceleration Programme delivered over 25,000 hours of targeted training for roles including product owners and scrum masters [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_160]. HSBC issued more than 42,000 digital credentials across data, digital, banking, finance, and wealth domains in 2025, supported by 46 newly launched digital badges [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_158].

### GRI 405 Diversity  
At year-end 2025, women held 34.7% of senior leadership roles globally, against an aspirational ambition of 35% [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_146]. Black heritage colleagues represented 3.0% of senior leadership roles in the UK and US combined, versus an ambition of 3.4% [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_146]. The Inclusion Index score — measured via the Snapshot employee engagement survey — reached 78%, exceeding the 75% ambition [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_146][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_66]. Among Board members at 31 December 2025, 62% identified as women and six (46%) as being from an ethnic minority background [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_588]. For executive management (Group Operating Committee and Group Head of Internal Audit), 23% were women and 32% identified as non-White [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_588]. In 2025, 69.1% of colleagues voluntarily self-identified their ethnic background [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_147].

### GRI 414 Supplier Social Assessment  
In 2025, 97.3% of approximately 9,830 contracted suppliers either confirmed adherence to HSBC’s refreshed Supplier Code of Conduct — which now includes principles on responsible AI use — or provided an alternative code accepted by HSBC’s Global Procurement function [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_179][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_168]. HSBC’s Global Procurement function continued implementing its human rights due diligence operating procedure, including supplier human rights audits and closure of findings from 2024 audits [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_166]. The Code sets minimum standards for suppliers on inclusion, human rights, and environmental performance [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_179].

### TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition)  
The context does not disclose HSBC’s assessment of the social impacts — such as workforce transitions, community vulnerability, or just transition planning — arising from its climate transition strategy. While HSBC references sustainability risk policies that consider human rights issues (e.g., forced labour, workers’ rights, health and safety of communities) in higher-risk sectors [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_167], and notes stakeholder consultations highlighted “the potential social impacts of AI on communities” [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_166], no specific analysis, metrics, or initiatives related to the social dimensions of climate transition are reported. There is no disclosure of alignment between workforce development programmes and net-zero goals, nor of community engagement on transition-related social risks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_160][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_166].

### GRI 403 Occupational Health & Safety  
HSBC reported 10 major injuries to employees in 2025 — defined as fractures, dislocations, concussions, loss of consciousness, or overnight hospital admission [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746]. The all-injury rate was 96 per 100,000 employees, up from 91 in 2024 and down from 110 in 2023 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746]. Lost days due to work injury totalled 331 in 2025, compared with 335 in 2024 and 594 in 2023 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746]. No workplace fatalities were recorded in 2025, 2024, or 2023, as the fatality rate is reported as “—” for all three years [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746]. In 2025, 33 named storms affected 2,222 buildings with no injuries or impact reported [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_746].

### GRI 404 Training  
In 2025, HSBC colleagues completed 5.6 million training hours, down from 6.2 million in 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_160]. This equated to 26.8 training hours per full-time equivalent (FTE) employee, versus 29.6 hours per FTE in 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_160]. Mandatory conduct training was completed by 99% of employees in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_66]. The Digital Acceleration Programme delivered over 25,000 hours of targeted training for roles including product owners and scrum masters [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_160]. HSBC issued more than 42,000 digital credentials across data, digital, banking, finance, and wealth domains in 2025, supported by 46 newly launched digital badges [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_158].

### GRI 405 Diversity  
At year-end 2025, women held 34.7% of senior leadership roles globally, against an aspirational ambition of 35% [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_146]. Black heritage colleagues represented 3.0% of senior leadership roles in the UK and US combined, versus an ambition of 3.4% [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_146]. The Inclusion Index score — measured via the Snapshot employee engagement survey — reached 78%, exceeding the 75% ambition [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_146][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_66]. Among Board members at 31 December 2025, 62% identified as women and six (46%) as being from an ethnic minority background [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_588]. For executive management (Group Operating Committee and Group Head of Internal Audit), 23% were women and 32% identified as non-White [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_588]. In 2025, 69.1% of colleagues voluntarily self-identified their ethnic background [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_147].

### GRI 414 Supplier Social Assessment  
In 2025, 97.3% of approximately 9,830 contracted suppliers either confirmed adherence to HSBC’s refreshed Supplier Code of Conduct — which now includes principles on responsible AI use — or provided an alternative code accepted by HSBC’s Global Procurement function [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_179][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_168]. HSBC’s Global Procurement function continued implementing its human rights due diligence operating procedure, including supplier human rights audits and closure of findings from 2024 audits [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_166]. The Code sets minimum standards for suppliers on inclusion, human rights, and environmental performance [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_179].

### TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition)  
The context does not disclose HSBC’s assessment of the social impacts — such as workforce transitions, community vulnerability, or just transition planning — arising from its climate transition strategy. While HSBC references sustainability risk policies that consider human rights issues (e.g., forced labour, workers’ rights, health and safety of communities) in higher-risk sectors [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_167], and notes stakeholder consultations highlighted “the potential social impacts of AI on communities” [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_166], no specific analysis, metrics, or initiatives related to the social dimensions of climate transition are reported. There is no disclosure of alignment between workforce development programmes and net-zero goals, nor of community engagement on transition-related social risks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_160][260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_166].

### Not covered in source material  
GRI 403: Occupational health policy scope (e.g., coverage of contractors or temporary staff); mental health metrics; definition of “employees” in injury reporting.  
GRI 404: Training breakdown by topic, demographic group, or seniority; investment in training as % of payroll; verification of completion rates.  
GRI 405: Representation data for LGBTQ+, disability, age, or religion; pay equity ratios or gap analyses; disaggregated promotion/retention rates.  
GRI 414: Supplier audit findings, tier-2 assessments, or capacity-building initiatives.

### Board Independence and Composition  
The Nomination & Corporate Governance Committee, acting on delegated authority from the Board, confirmed the independence of all non-executive Directors and the Group Chairman who stood for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. This assessment considered all circumstances likely to impair, or appear to impair, independence, in accordance with the UK and Hong Kong Corporate Governance Codes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Non-executive Directors serve initial three-year terms and typically two consecutive terms (six years); appointments beyond six years are subject to rolling one-year terms and rigorous review against the Board’s evolving needs [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. All Directors standing for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM were elected or re-elected by shareholders [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731].

### Conflicts of Interest Management  
HSBC maintains an annually reviewed conflicts of interest policy and procedures [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Directors must notify the Board of actual or potential conflicts and update it on changes to relevant facts or circumstances [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. They review and confirm their own and their closely associated persons’ outside interests twice yearly [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_733]. All conflicts are recorded in a formal register, and the Board authorised conflicts as they arose during 2025 under the Companies Act 2006 and HSBC Holdings’ Articles of Association [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Non-executive Directors undergo triennial re-vetting by the Group’s compliance team, including refreshed conflict checks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_733].

### Anti-Corruption and Integrity Framework  
HSBC’s global financial crime policy prohibits bribery and corruption and requires activity to be reasonable, transparent, appropriately documented, and authorised at an appropriate seniority level [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_174]. Risk-based due diligence and ongoing monitoring of customers and third parties are used to mitigate bribery and corruption risks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. In 2025, 99% of permanent and non-permanent employees completed mandatory financial crime training, including anti-bribery and corruption content — consistent with the 2024 rate [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. There were no concluded legal cases regarding bribery or corruption brought against HSBC or its employees in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175].

### Climate Risk Governance and Oversight  
The Board holds overall supervisory responsibility for HSBC’s ESG strategy, including climate risk governance, overseeing executive management on development, execution, and reporting [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_529]. The Group Chief Risk and Compliance Officer is the senior manager responsible for climate risk under the UK Senior Managers Regime [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_529]. The Group Risk Committee and Group Risk Management Meeting receive quarterly updates on climate risk indicators and oversee the Group’s climate risk profile and appetite [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_530]. The Group’s climate risk appetite statement forms part of the overarching risk appetite statement, is approved and overseen by the Board, and is reviewed annually—or sooner if breached [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_530].

### Whistleblowing and Speak-Up Mechanisms  
HSBC operates HSBC Confidential, a global whistleblowing channel managed by an independent third party in most markets, offering 24/7 hotlines and a multilingual web portal [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. In 2025, 1,100 concerns were investigated through this channel (2024: 925); 34% were substantiated (2024: 35%), and a further 19% identified other issues (2024: 22%) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. The Group Audit Committee oversees the effectiveness of the whistleblowing framework, and its Chair serves as HSBC’s Whistleblowers’ Champion [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_176].

### Board Committee Charters and Evaluation Methodology  
Board committees operate under formally defined terms of reference, available at www.hsbc.com/who-we-are/our-people/board-of-directors/board-committees [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_590]. The 2025 Board and committee performance review was facilitated internally by the Group Chief People & Governance Officer and Group Governance, following externally facilitated reviews in 2023 and 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_605]. It comprised a questionnaire and interviews with each Director and relevant senior management, focusing on progress against prior findings, oversight of organisational changes, and implementation of the How We Lead leadership framework [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_605]. The review concluded that the Board and its committees continued to operate effectively, with no material areas for improvement identified [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_606].

### Not covered in source material  
The source does not disclose any quantified, time-bound governance targets beyond the 2026 AI reporting initiative (e.g., no target for conflict register completeness, board-level climate competency coverage, or third-party anti-corruption audit frequency). GRI 205-1 disclosures on the number, scope, or findings of third-party anti-corruption audits — distinct from PwC’s financial audit — are absent. No information is provided on Board committee charters beyond their existence and public availability; specific mandates, authorities, or decision-making thresholds are not summarised. TCFD-specific disclosure of Board climate competency assessments, training participation rates, or curriculum details is not included.

### Board Independence and Composition  
The Nomination & Corporate Governance Committee, acting on delegated authority from the Board, confirmed the independence of all non-executive Directors and the Group Chairman who stood for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. This assessment considered all circumstances likely to impair, or appear to impair, independence, in accordance with the UK and Hong Kong Corporate Governance Codes [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Non-executive Directors serve initial three-year terms and typically two consecutive terms (six years); appointments beyond six years are subject to rolling one-year terms and rigorous review against the Board’s evolving needs [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731]. All Directors standing for election or re-election at the 2025 AGM were elected or re-elected by shareholders [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_731].

### Conflicts of Interest Management  
HSBC maintains an annually reviewed conflicts of interest policy and procedures [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Directors must notify the Board of actual or potential conflicts and update it on changes to relevant facts or circumstances [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. They review and confirm their own and their closely associated persons’ outside interests twice yearly [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_733]. All conflicts are recorded in a formal register, and the Board authorised conflicts as they arose during 2025 under the Companies Act 2006 and HSBC Holdings’ Articles of Association [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_732]. Non-executive Directors undergo triennial re-vetting by the Group’s compliance team, including refreshed conflict checks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_733].

### Anti-Corruption and Integrity Framework  
HSBC’s global financial crime policy prohibits bribery and corruption and requires activity to be reasonable, transparent, appropriately documented, and authorised at an appropriate seniority level [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_174]. Risk-based due diligence and ongoing monitoring of customers and third parties are used to mitigate bribery and corruption risks [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. In 2025, 99% of permanent and non-permanent employees completed mandatory financial crime training, including anti-bribery and corruption content — consistent with the 2024 rate [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. There were no concluded legal cases regarding bribery or corruption brought against HSBC or its employees in 2025 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175].

### Climate Risk Governance and Oversight  
The Board holds overall supervisory responsibility for HSBC’s ESG strategy, including climate risk governance, overseeing executive management on development, execution, and reporting [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_529]. The Group Chief Risk and Compliance Officer is the senior manager responsible for climate risk under the UK Senior Managers Regime [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_529]. The Group Risk Committee and Group Risk Management Meeting receive quarterly updates on climate risk indicators and oversee the Group’s climate risk profile and appetite [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_530]. The Group’s climate risk appetite statement forms part of the overarching risk appetite statement, is approved and overseen by the Board, and is reviewed annually—or sooner if breached [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_530].

### Whistleblowing and Speak-Up Mechanisms  
HSBC operates HSBC Confidential, a global whistleblowing channel managed by an independent third party in most markets, offering 24/7 hotlines and a multilingual web portal [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. In 2025, 1,100 concerns were investigated through this channel (2024: 925); 34% were substantiated (2024: 35%), and a further 19% identified other issues (2024: 22%) [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_175]. The Group Audit Committee oversees the effectiveness of the whistleblowing framework, and its Chair serves as HSBC’s Whistleblowers’ Champion [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_176].

### Board Committee Charters and Evaluation Methodology  
Board committees operate under formally defined terms of reference, available at www.hsbc.com/who-we-are/our-people/board-of-directors/board-committees [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_590]. The 2025 Board and committee performance review was facilitated internally by the Group Chief People & Governance Officer and Group Governance, following externally facilitated reviews in 2023 and 2024 [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_605]. It comprised a questionnaire and interviews with each Director and relevant senior management, focusing on progress against prior findings, oversight of organisational changes, and implementation of the How We Lead leadership framework [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_605]. The review concluded that the Board and its committees continued to operate effectively, with no material areas for improvement identified [260225-annual-report-and-accounts-2025 (1)_chunk_606].

### Not covered in source material  
The source does not disclose any quantified, time-bound governance targets beyond the 2026 AI reporting initiative (e.g., no target for conflict register completeness, board-level climate competency coverage, or third-party anti-corruption audit frequency). GRI 205-1 disclosures on the number, scope, or findings of third-party anti-corruption audits — distinct from PwC’s financial audit — are absent. No information is provided on Board committee charters beyond their existence and public availability; specific mandates, authorities, or decision-making thresholds are not summarised. TCFD-specific disclosure of Board climate competency assessments, training participation rates, or curriculum details is not included.
